question: What is the normal temperature range of a mercury-based clinical thermometer?
solution:
The correct answer is __35°C to 42°C.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The mercury-based clinical thermometer__ is a common instrument used to measure body temperature.
 
• The normal temperature range for a mercury-based clinical thermometer is 35°C to 42°C.
 
• This range is designed to measure human body temperature accurately and effectively.
 
• Temperatures outside this range are typically measured using specialized thermometers designed for other applications.
 
• Mercury thermometers are gradually being phased out due to environmental concerns associated with mercury.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Digital Thermometer:**

 
 
• Digital thermometers are now commonly used as an alternative to mercury thermometers.
 
• They provide faster readings and are safer as they do not contain mercury.
 
 
 
• **Infrared Thermometer:**
 
 
• Infrared thermometers can measure temperature from a distance without physical contact.
 
• These thermometers are widely used in medical, industrial, and environmental applications.
